title: Tony Jackson and stolen tunes
summary: They discuss Tony Jackson, whose music people copied, Pretty Baby, and his flamboyant dress.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, don't blame him, because people could steal it. I know Tony... I never knew Tony Jackson, but I knew Tony's sister I met here, Mrs. Sutter. And she said too that people would steal that music from Tony sometimes if he didn't care whether he had it published or not.
Irvin Barleen did a couple of pieces. Somebody took some of Tony's, I guess.
Really? Tony worked right next to Tony, a little one with a beer johnson. And Irvin used to come out here and sit for hours with Tony.
Listen to Tony. Pretty Baby and all that stuff. That's all Tony's.
Oh, yes. That was his biggest hit, I guess.
Yes. Pretty Baby. But this boy was very nice, he was a hit. And I would take down his numbers for him.
You see, he wore sort of sport clothes and all that.
Yes, a big bell-bottled pants. And a big hat. Mm-hmm. And he was very loud mouth.
But it was nice. I know you used to brag a lot, but still he was a wonderful musician, I thought. Oh, he was a wonderful musician. If I could have played like he did, I would brag too.
I don't think they'll ever have one that'll play right off the record like he did.
